extracted.intended_audience: literary-studies students, critics, and creative writers analyzing narrative craft
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Roland Barthes's five-code framework (Hermeneutic, Proairetic, Semantic, Symbolic, Referential) to analyze or evaluate narrative passages line-by-line, assessing how codes are activated, balanced, and interact to produce meaning and craft. Useful for close reading, literary criticism, and craft feedback for short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermeneutic Code (HER)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'voice of truth' — the mysteries, enigmas, and questions a narrative poses and gradually answers. Includes: posing the question (formulation); suspending the answer (delay, snare, partial answer, jamming); eventually disclosing (resolution). A narrative's suspense is built on the hermeneutic code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the passage formulates questions, how answers are delayed or obstructed, and how/when disclosure happens. Look for devices that prolong suspense (snare, partial answers, jamming) or that prematurely resolve enigmas. Consider HER's contribution to reader curiosity and narrative drive; note whether tension is maintained, dissipated, or closed off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proairetic Code (ACT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'voice of empirics' — the actions and behavioral sequences. Names of actions ('decision,' 'departure,' 'meeting,' 'battle') that the reader recognizes as conventional units. Drives plot forward through chains of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify discrete action-units and chains that create expectations of 'what happens next.' Assess whether actions are clearly signaled and whether they form compelling proairetic sequences. A text dominated by proairetic coding reads as plot-driven; consider whether this yields narrative propulsion or thinness of meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic Code (SEM)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'voice of the person' — the connotations attached to characters, objects, settings (a character's name evokes wealth; a setting's color evokes mood). The flicker of meanings around any narrative element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map recurring connotations and semantic fields that cluster around characters, objects, or motifs. Evaluate how accumulated connotation builds character depth and atmosphere. Note subtle semantic 'flickers' that suggest traits without explicit statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic Code (SYM)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'voice of symbol' — the larger thematic oppositions and binaries that organize the work (life/death, light/dark, masculine/feminine, inside/outside). Symbols cluster into structuring antitheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate binary oppositions and their symbolic clustering. Assess whether oppositions are generative (productive) — producing thematic nuance — or schematic (flat). Consider SYM's role as the deep structure of meaning and how it shapes the work's thematic resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural / Referential Code (REF)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'voice of science' — references to bodies of knowledge outside the text (medicine, history, geography, gossip, common sense). The text relies on the reader's cultural literacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify references to external knowledges, institutions, or shared cultural assumptions. Evaluate how effectively REF anchors the narrative in a recognisable social/cultural world and how shifts in cultural literacy might alter meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codes Interaction / Layered Orchestration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any narrative passage simultaneously activates multiple codes; a single sentence may pose a hermeneutic question, name an action (proairetic), connote a character trait (semantic), invoke a binary (symbolic), and rely on cultural reference. The art of fiction is the layered orchestration of these codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess passages for multi-code activation and how layers combine to produce complexity. Look for moments where codes reinforce each other or where tension arises from competing activations. Close-reading should track co-occurrence and stacking of codes at the sentence and paragraph level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional Pairings (HER+ACT; SEM+SYM+REF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pairings Barthes highlights: HER + ACT produce internal chronology and plot drive; SEM + SYM + REF produce connotative depth and thematic resonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these pairings diagnostically: evaluate whether plot momentum (HER+ACT) and connotative/thematic depth (SEM+SYM+REF) are balanced, or whether one axis dominates. Consider how pairings contribute to pacing, meaning, and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality of the Text (writerly vs readerly)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'writerly' (scriptible) text foregrounds the plurality of codes — the reader actively constructs meaning. A 'readerly' (lisible) text suppresses plurality — meaning is delivered. A readerly text is more accessible; a writerly text is more profound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the degree to which the text invites active interpretation (multi-coded, ambiguous, productive) versus delivering a single, digested meaning. Use this axis to judge accessibility versus depth and to recommend editorial choices depending on audience/goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which codes the text activates
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which of the five codes (HER/ACT/SEM/SYM/REF) are present in the passage or work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make an inventory of activated codes at various granularities (line, paragraph, scene). Use presence/absence mapping as the first step of analysis; report notable absences as well as activations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Richness of activation in each code
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how rich the activation is in each code — the density and elaboration of hermeneutic questions, action chains, connotative fields, symbolic oppositions, and referential material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score or describe density (sparse → rich) for each code. Richness signals layered meaning; sparse activation suggests thinness in that dimension. Consider both frequency and complexity of manifestations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization vs contention among codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the codes harmonize or contend — whether they support a unified reading or generate tensions and competing meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note where codes align to reinforce themes and where they produce productive contradictions. Use this criterion to judge coherence, ambivalence, or deliberate instability in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermeneutic tension management
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the hermeneutic code maintains tension or releases it prematurely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate pacing of revelations and obstructions. Identify techniques that prolong mystery or that resolve it; judge whether the timing of disclosure enhances suspense and thematic payoff or undercuts them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productive vs schematic symbolic oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether symbolic oppositions are productive (generate thematic nuance) or schematic (flat, merely classificatory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how binaries are complicated, inverted, or interrogated vs. used as simple labels. Reward symbolic work that multiplies meaning rather than merely signaling an obvious contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density, balance, and dominance as craft indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: A short story can be coded line-by-line for HER/ACT/SEM/SYM/REF activation. Density and balance reveal craft level: a story dominated only by the proairetic (action) reads as plot-driven but thin; one rich in all five reads as literary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a comparative or quantitative readout (line counts, frequency tags, qualitative notes) to show balance. Diagnose over-reliance (e.g., excessive ACT) and suggest enrichment strategies (introduce SEM/SYM/REF layers or hermeneutic tension) to increase craft.
